_what_this_is: Offline-verifiable evidence for the knowledge-base finding in the accompanying article: a vector-store ingestion node configured to insert (with clear-before-insert not enabled) APPENDS an edited document alongside its previous version rather than replacing it. Captured before the scratch index and all API keys were revoked. Contains everything needed to reproduce the retrieval result WITHOUT any live service: the query embedding, both stored vectors, their metadata, and the vector database's returned scores.

provenance.specimen: A widely-installed public RAG chatbot template (Drive-to-vector-store, identified by function, not by id or author)
provenance.index: [scratch index name redacted] - 3072 dimensions, cosine metric, deleted after this export
provenance.embedding_model: models/gemini-embedding-001. Substituted for the model the template ships with, which its provider retired on 2026-01-14; the substitution is disclosed in the article and does not affect this finding, which concerns insert semantics rather than embedding quality.
provenance.question: How many weeks of paid parental leave are employees entitled to?
provenance.sequence: policy v1 (12 weeks) ingested -> queried -> the SAME document edited to v2 (20 weeks) -> re-ingested through the template's own insert node -> index went from 1 vector to 2
provenance.capture_method: Live query against the index, capturing the query embedding and both stored vectors in full

independent_recomputation.text: Parental leave policy. Employees are entitled to 20 weeks of paid parental leave.
Parental leave policy. Employees are entitled to 12 weeks of paid parental leave.

verification.recomputation_method: cosine = dot(query, stored); both query and stored vectors are unit-normalised (norm 1.000000), so dot product IS cosine. Method verified correct.

residual.magnitude: ~1.9e-4 to 2.9e-4; agrees to 3 decimal places, differs in the 4th
residual.float32_quantization_tested: does NOT explain it - round-tripping either vector through float32 leaves the delta unchanged
residual.likely_cause_UNPROVEN: The database appears to score against a lossy internal representation while returning a higher-precision copy of the vectors. Consistent with compressed serverless indexes. NOT established - stated as a hypothesis, not a fact.
residual.does_it_affect_the_finding: No. The finding rests on: two vectors present where one document was ingested; both retrieved for the same query; near-identical relevance. Rank order is preserved and the GAP between the two reproduces - database 0.002953 vs recomputed 0.003045.

metadata.text: Parental leave policy. Employees are entitled to 20 weeks of paid parental leave.
Parental leave policy. Employees are entitled to 12 weeks of paid parental leave.

_how_to_verify: Both vectors are unit-normalised, so cosine == dot product. Recompute dot(query_embedding.values, stored_vectors[i].values). Expect ~0.8488 and ~0.8457, which agree with the database's returned 0.8485 / 0.8455 to 3 decimal places. See verification.residual for the unexplained 4th-decimal difference - it does not bear on the finding.
